content:
The woman dubbed "Mom of the Year" by the San Francisco Giants broadcast team in a viral video—and who sparked widespread online backlash against her husband—has now come forward to publicly defend her husband.

The couple and their daughter became a viral talking point when, on Tuesday just past, the woman was filmed on the Oracle Park stairs carrying a baby in her arms along with several takeout food containers as she made her way down, while her husband appeared completely unfazed and began tucking into the food, watching his wife struggle.

The broadcast team of commentators Duane Kuiper and Mike Krukow hailed the woman for her multitasking prowess, calling her an "Olympic champion" and "Mom of the Year." The pair portrayed her husband as a thoughtless deadbeat who only cared about ketchup—and internet users felt the same way.

So the woman, who goes by Erika and has not disclosed her surname, decided to hit back hard.

In a Substack post published on 25 September, she wrote: "Millions of people have seen the clip of me carrying our daughter and the food back to our seats. They crowned me 'Mom of the Year' and piled on my husband with every insult under the sun. Some even slid into my DMs or posted TikToks saying I should leave him."

She continued: "My name is Erika, our daughter is Anastasia, and my husband is Ramses. Before you pass judgment on what our marriage looks like, I'd like you to hear from the very woman you're rushing to defend."

Erika went on at length in the post to clear her husband's name, writing:

"Ramses is an incredible husband and an even better father. We've been together nine years and are currently raising two children under two. I know exactly how he treats me, how he loves our kids, and what he's given up for this family. A piece of conversation the audience couldn't hear somehow became the basis for millions of people to judge our marriage."

She wrote that, as she understood it, Ramses had originally offered to hold Anastasia so that Erika could go to the restroom (he later said it was to go get food). He had also asked if she wanted to eat first and whether he should take the takeout containers. She turned him down every time—and at that moment, she wrote, he was grieving the loss of a friend.

She wrote: "Our marriage gives either of us permission to ask for help. That night, I chose to look after him. The camera caught a moment of me stepping up for my husband, but it didn't show the countless times he's done the same for me."
